newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FOCUS-Taiwan interbank rate soars to record high.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Taiwan interbank rate soars to record high.

text.p: Taiwan's interbank rate roared into double digits to a record high close on Friday despite central bank stabilisation efforts, as funds continued to stream out of banks into the red-hot stock market.
The overnight interbank rate, capping a 10-session ascent, closed at 10.541 percent against Thursday's 8.597 finish -- roughly double the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
It was the rate's highest close since official recordings began on September 1, 1991.

Dealers said the central bank's T$8.25 billion dollars ($9 million) afternoon fund injection did little to relieve the acute liquidity squeeze and predicted further gains if the bank refrained from more drastic measures.
The 30-day commercial paper also surged, closing at 10.00-11.00 percent compared to Thursday's 8.25-8.75.
Both rates have skyrocketed in recent weeks on a torrent of funds flowing from the banking system into a sizzling stock market that has gained almost 800 points or 10 percent in July alone.
Showing no signs of slowing, the weighted index jumped 112.83 points or 1.27 percent on Friday to notch yet another seven-year high close at 8,984.59.
Friday's turnover was hectic at T$182 billion, but still well below the all-time high T$251 billion set on July 19.
Dealers said investors were disappointed by the central bank's T$8.25 billion injection because they had expected a much bigger intervention.
"The market was expecting an injection of around T$30 billion, but apparently the central bank was unwilling to solve the liquidity with one quick injection," said one dealer.
"If the central bank does not launch more actions tomorrow, the rates will rise further," he added.
The central bank vowed to keep a close eye on the banking system's liquidity flows, but did not say whether it would step up loosening measures.
The bank had said on Tuesday that it did not plan to cut reserve requirements because "the current tight liquidity will not last long."
In the bond market, the benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 5.9000 percent against Monday's 5.8850 close. ($ = 27.82 Taiwan Dollars)
